title: AWS Cost Calculator
summary: Built and enhanced an AWS cost-calculation platform that converts infrastructure configurations into normalized pricing models and supports reliable cost estimation across multiple product surfaces.
description: The AWS Cost Calculator helps teams estimate infrastructure costs before provisioning resources. The platform normalizes service configuration data, retrieves and transforms pricing information, and supports reusable estimation workflows for dashboards, CI/CD processes and infrastructure planning.
responsibilities: Developed backend functionality supporting infrastructure cost-estimation workflows.
Designed configuration-normalization logic for EC2, S3 and EKS estimation scenarios.
Transformed AWS Price List API data into deterministic internal pricing models.
Supported reusable cost-estimation flows across multiple product surfaces.
Improved reliability of cost calculations for infrastructure planning scenarios.
Contributed to what-if estimation workflows for CI/CD and Infrastructure as Code use cases.
challenges: Different services exposed configuration data in inconsistent formats.
Raw pricing data required transformation before it could be used reliably.
Estimation workflows needed to remain consistent across multiple interfaces.
Infrastructure scenarios required deterministic results before actual provisioning.
solutions: Created normalized infrastructure blueprints for EC2, S3 and EKS.
Built a deterministic Price List API processing pipeline.
Separated raw pricing retrieval from reusable estimation models.
Designed reusable calculation flows for dashboard and automated estimation scenarios.
outcomes: Improved pricing and forecasting reliability by approximately 30–50%.
Reduced the time required to model infrastructure changes by approximately 80%.
Enabled consistent estimation logic across multiple product surfaces.
Supported cost planning before infrastructure provisioning.

title: AWS Native Services Platform
summary: Developed a high-performance asynchronous backend and resource-intelligence platform covering more than 250 AWS services, with inventory discovery, metadata enrichment, pricing insights and bulk exports.
description: The platform provides centralized visibility into native AWS resources across accounts and regions. It discovers resources, normalizes service-specific information, enriches records with metadata and cost information, and exposes the resulting data through REST APIs and dashboard workflows.
responsibilities: Launched an asynchronous FastAPI microservice backend using aioboto3.
Developed service-specific resource discovery and mapping workflows.
Built a native-services engine covering more than 250 AWS services.
Added metadata enrichment, hardware metrics and per-resource pricing information.
Implemented CSV and JSON bulk export pipelines.
Supported account-wide and organization-wide resource inventory workflows.
Optimized asynchronous service calls and backend response handling.
challenges: AWS services return highly inconsistent resource structures.
Resource collection across many services can create high API latency.
Large inventories require efficient normalization and export handling.
Pricing and hardware metadata must be matched with discovered resources.
Multi-region resource visibility requires reliable asynchronous processing.
solutions: Implemented asynchronous resource-discovery workflows with FastAPI and aioboto3.
Created reusable mapping and normalization layers for service-specific data.
Added metadata and FinOps enrichment after resource discovery.
Built bulk CSV and JSON export pipelines.
Optimized request concurrency and backend processing paths.
outcomes: Reduced API latency by more than 60%.
Covered more than 250 AWS services.
Improved cost-transparency accuracy by approximately 40%.
Reduced console-navigation overhead by more than 70%.
Accelerated audit workflows by approximately 3×.

title: Amazon Q Cost Analytics Assistant
summary: Built a reusable floating AI assistant for three cost-dashboard views, enabling users to ask contextual billing questions, select dashboard elements and safely apply chat-generated filters after confirmation.
description: The assistant is integrated across Cost Analytics, Cost Explorer and Cost DrillDown. It combines natural-language queries with current dashboard context so users can investigate costs without manually navigating multiple filters and views. Selection mode attaches supported chart, service, account or cost-driver metadata to a question. A two-step workflow answers first and applies proposed dashboard filters only after user confirmation.
responsibilities: Developed a global floating assistant reusable across three dashboard routes.
Implemented persistent conversation handling through conversation_id.
Built selection mode for more than 10 dashboard element types.
Passed selected chart, service, account and cost-driver metadata into chat requests.
Implemented confirmation-based dashboard updates.
Improved backend intent parsing and action execution.
Added support for multiple billing-query categories.
Reused dashboard data services so assistant values remain consistent with the UI.
Added Markdown rendering for sufficiently detailed responses.
Integrated assistant-generated filters with existing Angular dashboard state.
challenges: A plain text query often lacks enough context to identify the chart or service the user means.
Automatically changing dashboard filters can create confusing or unexpected UI behavior.
Assistant responses must match values already shown in the dashboard.
Different billing views expose different metadata and UI structures.
Query parsing must distinguish informational answers from dashboard actions.
solutions: Added interactive selection mode and contextual UI metadata.
Created a reusable assistant integration shared by three routes.
Used a two-step answer-and-confirm workflow before applying filters.
Reused the same internal data services as the dashboard.
Extended intent parsing for cost lookup, dates, spikes and recommendations.
Maintained conversation continuity through conversation IDs.
outcomes: Reusable across 3 billing dashboard routes.
Persistent conversation state using conversation_id.
Context-aware selection mode for 10+ UI element types.
Two-step confirmation-based dashboard updates.
Support for 5+ billing-query categories.
Markdown formatting for detailed responses.
Consistent values between assistant responses and dashboard data by using shared internal services.
supported_scenarios: Context-aware questions about selected UI elements

title: Documentation and Attachment Management Module
summary: Built an eight-endpoint Spring Boot module for managing notes, attachments and additional links with validation, soft deletion and controlled file handling.
description: The module provides note-management and attachment-management workflows through REST APIs. It supports creating and updating notes, retrieving content, soft-deleting notes, uploading and listing attachments, deleting attachments and managing additional links.
responsibilities: Built eight REST API endpoints.
Implemented create, read, update and soft-delete note workflows.
Added attachment upload, listing and deletion functionality.
Implemented tenant-aware data isolation across three roles.
Added account, creator and tenant ownership checks.
Integrated S3-backed attachment handling.
Implemented file-size and file-type validation.
Added additional-link storage and deduplication.
Implemented soft-deletion behavior for attachments.
challenges: Notes and attachments required coordinated lifecycle handling.
File uploads needed strict size and format validation.
Updated notes could re-upload existing attachments unintentionally.
Deleted attachments needed consistent soft-delete handling.
Additional links required deduplication.
solutions: Separated note and attachment operations into structured service workflows.
Enforced a 25 MB upload limit.
Restricted uploads to 11 allowed file types.
Added attachment-listing and attachment-deletion endpoints.
Added additional-link deduplication.
Used soft-deletion fields to preserve data history.
outcomes: Delivered 8 REST endpoints.
Enforced a 25 MB attachment limit and 11 allowed file types.
Supported create, update, retrieve and soft-delete workflows.
Delivered attachment upload, listing and deletion.
Prevented duplicate additional links.

title: Distributed Multi-Drone AI Tracking System
summary: Designed a distributed real-time tracking system in which edge devices handled video capture and flight control while an NVIDIA Jetson performed multi-stream object detection and tracking.
description: The system combined multiple RTSP camera streams, real-time object detection, pixel tracking and autonomous flight-control commands. Computationally intensive inference was offloaded to an NVIDIA Jetson, while a Raspberry Pi communicated with the flight controller.
responsibilities: Designed a distributed edge-computing architecture.
Used Python and MAVSDK for flight-control integration.
Offloaded YOLOv8 inference to an NVIDIA Jetson.
Used a Raspberry Pi for real-time autonomous flight control.
Built a multi-stream video-processing pipeline.
Decoded and processed multiple 1280×960 RTSP feeds.
Integrated GStreamer and NVIDIA DeepStream.
Used NvDCF for pixel tracking.
Built a 10 Hz UDP communication bridge.
Transmitted PID-calculated velocity vectors through MAVLink.
Added asynchronous state machines and network-loss failsafes.
Implemented timeout-to-hover behavior.
challenges: Multiple high-resolution RTSP streams required efficient decoding.
Inference and flight control needed to run on different devices.
Network loss could make autonomous movement unsafe.
Detection coordinates had to be translated into flight-control commands.
Real-time tracking required low-latency communication.
solutions: Distributed processing between the Jetson and Raspberry Pi.
Used DeepStream and GStreamer for accelerated video handling.
Transmitted control vectors over a 10 Hz UDP bridge.
Used PID calculations for target-centering commands.
Added asynchronous state handling.
Implemented timeout-to-hover failsafes during network loss.
outcomes: Processed multiple 1280×960 RTSP streams.
Established 10 Hz UDP control communication.
Created a distributed Jetson and Raspberry Pi architecture.
Integrated real-time YOLOv8 detection and NvDCF tracking.
Added a timeout-to-hover network failsafe.

title: Air Pollution Prediction Platform
summary: Developed a research-based machine-learning platform for air-pollution prediction using regression and classification workflows with clear analytical result presentation.
description: The platform translates published air-quality research into a practical Python workflow for preparing environmental data, comparing regression and classification approaches, and presenting predictions through an accessible analytical interface concept.
responsibilities: Prepared and cleaned environmental datasets.
Developed repeatable preprocessing workflows.
Compared regression and classification approaches.
Evaluated model behavior with appropriate metrics.
Designed a responsive analytical interface concept for presenting results.
Connected the implementation to published research.
challenges: Environmental measurements contain noise, gaps and multiple interacting factors.
Regression and classification results require different evaluation approaches.
Technical predictions needed to remain understandable to non-specialist users.
solutions: Created a consistent data-cleaning and preprocessing pipeline.
Used comparative model evaluation for prediction tasks.
Structured results around clear metrics and visual explanations.
Translated the research workflow into a usable platform concept.
outcomes: Delivered repeatable air-pollution prediction workflows.
Supported both regression and classification analysis.
Turned published research into a practical analytical platform concept.
Improved the clarity of model-result presentation.
